absent: Implementations of the common acquire and release and sync primitives behind the reporting wrappers.
Dependency graph construction and deadlock and ordering violation detection.
Chain hash function and cache lookup and eviction policy.
Conversion between interrupt contexts beyond hash restart and usage tracking.
Mutex blocking slow paths and waiter queueing and wakeup and ownership transfer.
Percpu reader-writer read-side and write-side lock and unlock behavior.
Optimistic queue enqueue and dequeue and spinning protocol beyond init and locked test.
Lockref reference counting transitions for get and put and deletion beyond init and liveness tests.
Raw spinlock and rwlock hardware primitives and memory ordering guarantees.
Realtime mutex base semantics and priority handling.

findings.text: The checker records acquisition in three sharing modes called exclusive and shared and shared-recursive through one common acquire path with a matching release path. Each primitive family provides small conveniences for its normal and nested and read cases, where nested forms carry an extra cookie and read forms for read-write locks pick shared or shared-recursive depending on a recursion predicate, while sequence counters always use shared-recursive for reads.

Generic map helpers report read acquisition in normal and try variants using the shared-recursive mode at the current program position, and a separate sync helper reports a synchronization point for a map at the current position.

Active validation helpers briefly mark a lock as acquired and then released to let the checker verify ordering, with separate forms for normal and read and subclass-nested checks that consult the dep_map member of the supplied lock.

Checking is considered enabled only when global debug locks are on and per-cpu recursion is not active. When enabled, one-shot warnings assert expected interrupt and preemption context, covering interrupts enabled and disabled and hard interrupt context and absence of hard interrupt context and preemption enabled and disabled with zero preempt count and hard interrupt flag, plus soft interrupt context without hard interrupt or nonmaskable context.

When the checker is compiled out, the validation helpers and all interrupt and preemption and soft interrupt assertions including the soft interrupt function variant become empty operations that accept their arguments and do nothing.

On realtime builds an additional assertion warns when hard interrupt context is observed outside threaded or configured interrupt handling without recursion, while non-realtime builds provide an empty operation with the same name.
A hook for suspicious read-copy-update use accepts file and line and message information and performs no action in these fragments.

The subclass limit named MAX_LOCKDEP_SUBCLASSES is 8. Wait ordering is LD_WAIT_INV and LD_WAIT_FREE and LD_WAIT_SPIN and LD_WAIT_CONFIG and LD_WAIT_SLEEP and LD_WAIT_MAX, where the config entry aliases the spin entry when raw nesting proof is disabled. Lock ordering is LD_LOCK_NORMAL and LD_LOCK_PERCPU and LD_LOCK_WAIT_OVERRIDE and LD_LOCK_MAX.
The constant XXX_LOCK_USAGE_STATES is 2 and LOCK_TRACE_STATES is four times the former plus two.
Caching classes named NR_LOCKDEP_CACHING_CLASSES count 2 and lock statistic points named LOCKSTAT_POINTS count 4.
Key bits named MAX_LOCKDEP_KEYS_BITS are 13 and key capacity named MAX_LOCKDEP_KEYS is one shifted left by that bit count, while the initial chain key named INITIAL_CHAIN_KEY is negative one.
The optimistic queue unlocked value named OSQ_UNLOCKED_VAL is 0 and the lockref dead value named __LOCKREF_DEAD_VAL is negative 128.

A subclass key holds a single byte and is packed. A class key in its full form is a union of a hash node named hash_entry and an array named subkeys sized by the subclass limit, while its empty form carries no members.

Comparison callbacks take two maps and return an integer, while print callbacks take one map and return nothing. The class record links by hash_entry and lock_entry and tracks dependencies with locks_after and locks_before. It references a subclass key and the two callbacks and stores subclass with dep_gen_id and usage_mask with usage_traces sized by trace states and name with name_version and inner and outer wait types with lock type, plus optional contention points. Layout randomization is disabled for this record.

Timing named lock_time holds min and max and total and nr. Bounce ordering named bounce_type is bounce_acquired_write and bounce_acquired_read and bounce_contended_write and bounce_contended_read and nr_bounce_types, with bounce_acquired aliasing acquired write and bounce_contended aliasing contended write. Statistics hold contention_point and contending_point with read_waittime and write_waittime and read_holdtime and write_holdtime and bounces.

A full map holds key and class_cache sized by caching classes and name with outer and inner wait types and lock type and optional cpu with ip. A pin cookie holds val. A held lock records prev_chain_key with acquire_ip and instance with nest_lock and optional waittime_stamp with holdtime_stamp and class_idx sized by key bits and irq_context of 2 bits with trylock of 1 and read of 2 and check of 1 and hardirqs_off of 1 and sync of 1 and references of 11 and pin_count of 24 with seq_count of 8. Empty map and cookie forms carry no members.

Selection named USE_CMPXCHG_LOCKREF is true only with architecture support and symmetric multiprocessing and spinlock size within 4. The reference is a union of combined 64-bit lock_count or a spinlock named lock with integer named count. Dead marking uses negative 128.
Initialization prepares the spinlock and sets count to 1. Liveness checks read count once and report dead when equal to the dead value, with a second check also treating 0 as terminal.

One initializer validates the argument and assigns a static subclass key with a name and LD_WAIT_CONFIG through a raw init. A second initializer validates and assigns an unlocked value directly. A realtime initializer delegates to an inner init with false.
Non-realtime mutex storage holds owner and wait_lock with optional osq and first_waiter guarded by wait_lock and optional magic with dep_map. Realtime storage holds rtmutex with optional dep_map.
Dep map initialization either sets name with LD_WAIT_SLEEP or expands to nothing. Debug initialization either stores a magic self reference or expands to nothing with destroy as an empty operation.

Static definition creates a mutex from an initializer, with normal storage starting from zero owner and unlocked wait lock and NULL first waiter, and realtime storage from a realtime base initializer. Runtime init forwards name and key to lockdep or generic or realtime variants, and keyed init supplies stringified name. A locked test consults the realtime base.
Device-managed init returns 0 without registering destroy when debug is off. A return helper initializes a mutex and yields it, and a device helper combines both steps.

Blocking acquisition provides plain and interruptible and killable and I/O forms defaulting to 0 subclass, plus nest-lock forms that validate a second dep_map and killable nested forms that accept subclass or nest cookie.
When nesting proof is unavailable, all nested and nest-lock spellings collapse to their plain counterparts, ignoring subclass and nest arguments.
Nonblocking acquisition offers a nest-lock form validating a second dep_map and a plain form passing NULL, with a fallback spelling that ignores the nest argument.
Scoped guard constructors exist for plain and try and interruptible and killable and init flavors, each mapping to a common with-guard attribute helper.

The optimistic queue stores a tail encoding the queued cpu or unlocked when empty, with a static unlocked initializer and runtime init setting unlocked and a locked test comparing tail against unlocked.

Per-cpu reader-writer state holds rss and read_count with writer and waiters and block and optional dep_map. Dep map init either sets name or expands to nothing. Static definition creates a per-cpu counter and initializes sync with count and writer with waiters and 0 block.
Each header defines a unique include guard macro to prevent multiple inclusion.

Reentrancy during checking must be excluded via the recursion guard, otherwise assertions may warn spuriously. Interrupt context crossings reset chain separation to avoid false dependencies. A lockref showing dead or zero must not be treated as live. Mutex waiter linkage requires holding the wait lock.

Held tracking starts from an initial chain key and accumulates a one-way hash per acquisition, restarting from zero on entry to hard or soft interrupt context. Each entry records sharing and try and check and sync flags with reference and pin and sequence counts that evolve across acquire and release and pin operations.
